body: **Summary:** Life insurers earn the margin embedded in each policy sold, measured as VNB, plus the unwind of their embedded value. Protection and non-par savings carry the highest margins, ULIPs the lowest. General insurers earn underwriting result plus investment float. Key metrics for life: APE growth, VNB margin, VNB growth, persistency (13th/61st month), product mix, EV growth and operating RoEV, banca concentration. For general: combined ratio, loss ratio, solvency and market share. Cycle drivers: equity markets (ULIP demand), interest rates (non-par pricing), tax changes (Feb 2023 Budget taxed policies above ₹5 lakh premium), IRDAI rules (surrender-value norms from Oct 2024, commission caps) and GST (individual life and health exempted from Sep 2025, losing input tax credit). Lead indicators: monthly IRDAI/Life Council new business premium, GI Council monthly premium data, bancassurance partner growth. Winners built proprietary distribution plus a diversified bank partner, balanced their product mix and kept persistency high. Losers depended on one bank partner, chased ULIP volumes in bull markets, or were LIC losing share. Valuation: P/EV. Private life insurers listed in 2016–17 at roughly 3–5x EV, de-rated to about 2–3x after the 2023 tax change. GIs trade on P/E or P/B. Nov 2026: H1 FY27 VNB is growing (ICICI Pru +22.3%, HDFC Life +12%, Bajaj Life margin 19.2%), but the GST ITC loss costs ~60–100 bps of margin. Traps: APE growth without VNB, and the GST and surrender-rule effects on reported margins. Sources: [1](https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/hdfc-life-insurance-share-price-in-focus-as-company-announces-q2-fy27-results/) · [2](https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/hdfc-life-q1-fy-27-results-net-profit-vnb-july-2026/) · [3](https://www.investywise.com/icici-life-insurance-limited-announces-earnings-call-transcript-for-h1-fy2027/) · [4](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/bajaj-life-margin-retail-lag-ppt-cmw1lsh1700co31qlernq6z3p)

body: **Summary:** Auto component makers supply OEMs (domestic and global) and the aftermarket. Profit depends on content per vehicle times OEM volumes, with commodity pass-through lagging by about a quarter. The aftermarket and replacement segment (tyres, batteries, filters) carries better margins and is less cyclical. Key metrics: revenue growth against underlying OEM production (outperformance shows content gains), order book and lifetime-value wins, EBITDA margin, RoCE, export share and geography, EV/powertrain-agnostic share, customer concentration, and working capital. Cycle drivers: domestic OEM cycles, global auto production (Europe and US trucks matter for forgings), tariffs (25% US tariff on Indian auto parts from 2025, Section 232), the EV transition shrinking ICE content, and the China+1 sourcing shift. Lead indicators: SIAM and Vahan, S&P Global Light Vehicle Production forecasts, US Class 8 truck orders (ACT Research), ACMA half-yearly data, EU registrations. Winners (Motherson via acquisitions-plus-integration, Uno Minda and Endurance via content-per-vehicle gains, Sona via EV-agnostic driveline) grew faster than OEM volumes, diversified customers and kept RoCE above 15%. Losers were single-customer suppliers, ICE-only powertrain parts, and debt-funded overseas acquisitions (Amtek Auto). Valuation: P/E 20–40x for growth and EV names, 12–20x for cyclical exporters. Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 results were Sona revenue +35% (EV >50% of sales) with PAT +29%, and Sundram PAT +13%. New US contracts were in limbo due to tariffs (ACMA). Traps: order-book 'lifetime value', and EV hype multiples. Sources: [1](https://www.autocarpro.in/news/sona-comstar-net-profit-rises-29-percent-to-rs-223-crore-in-q2-fy27-135474) · [2](https://www.autocarpro.in/news/sundram-fasteners-q2-net-profit-rises-14-percent-to-rs-160-crore-as-revenue-expands-135542) · [3](https://www.autocarpro.in/news/new-supply-contracts-to-us-in-limbo-amid-tariff-woes-acma-130598) · [4](https://www.businesstoday.in/auto/story/auto-industry-posts-record-october-sales-as-passenger-vehicles-cross-5-lakh-mark-2-wheelers-grow-16-567320-2026-11-13)

body:
- **Reports:** the latest 5 ARs per symbol from `nse_fetch.annual_reports`. One row per FY; a later "Revised" upload wins. Each AR is dated at its NSE submission date. ZIPs (FY22-FY23) are read in memory and only `*.pdf` members are used. The PDFs are deleted after `pdftotext -layout`.
- **Zone:** the Chairman's/MD's message, the Board's (Directors') Report, the MD&A, and the energy-conservation/technology-absorption annexure. Report-level headings count only in the first 8 lines of a page. Two-column pages are split. Tables are rebuilt row by row.
- **Promises:** `candidates.py` (unchanged), then the rule builder in `ar_run.py`. A statement is kept only if (a) the company is the subject, (b) it is not macro or industry text, (c) it has a project or target word, and (d) it has a future marker. Chain key = `asset:milestone`.
- **Evidence:** later ARs' sentences on the same asset, classified done / pending / dropped and dated.
- **As-of date:** 2026-11-23. Cache: scratchpad `ar_mode/` (the text only; it is not kept in git).
- **Hand reads:** for GULFPETRO and REPRO, every sentence with a broad forward marker in the AR text before the auditors' report (`scripts_ar_mode/handread_dump.py`; independent of the zone and promise rules), read and judged by hand. This yielded 90 and 148 sentences. The SUNFLAG baseline is the ledger built by hand on the same day (`SUNFLAG_live.md` section 5.4).
title: AR_mode_validation › 1. Method

body:
**Task rule:** universe = `research_notes/Backtests/india_pead_live/universe.csv`, non-financial, market cap ₹1,000–20,000 cr (inside base-rate
class `india_nonfin_1000_20000cr_5y`) at the latest NSE close; trailing EV/EBITDA and P/E from screener consolidated data for a random sample of
120 (`random.Random(20261125)`); keep the CHEAPEST tercile on EV/EBITDA (exclude negative EBITDA); shuffle the tercile with
`random.Random(20261126)`; the first company passing the stage-2 filters (v3) is the subject.

**Operational definitions** were written to `live_dd3/prereg_selection.md` (scratchpad) *before* the frame was built or any ratio seen:
1. Latest close = NSE bhavcopy `sec_bhavdata_full_23112026.csv` (23-Nov-2026 close, published by 18:00 IST). Mcap = universe shares × close.
2. Financials out = NSE index industry "Financial Services" (29) + the live-dd1 hand list (39 in range) + any new unclassified name judged
   financial (the two new no-industry names, APLLTD = Alembic Pharma and SUBEXLTD = Subex, are non-financial).
3. Eligible list sorted alphabetically → `random.Random(20261125).sample(eligible, 120)`.
4. Screener `/company/<SYM>/consolidated/` + the "Other Assets" schedule API. EBITDA_TTM = Σ last 4 quarterly "Operating Profit" (ex other
   income); PAT_TTM = Σ last 4 "Net Profit"; net debt = last Borrowings − last "Cash Equivalents"; EV = mcap + net debt. "Financing Profit"
   P&L format → financial, dropped.
5. Valid = EBITDA_TTM > 0; tercile = first ceil(n/3) by EV/EBITDA ascending.
6. Tercile sorted alphabetically → `random.Random(20261126).shuffle` → walk.
7. Stage-2 v3 checks in order: scoreability (entity exists through 2027-09-30), fraud-judgment flags, pledge ≤ 50% (NSE pledge API, SHP XBRL
   fallback), no qualified audit / auditor exit, not in the PEAD avoid window (63 trading days before 23-Nov-2026 → window starts 21-Aug-2026),
   solvency screen not red.

**How it ran** (scripts `live_dd3/scripts/frame.py`, `sample.py`, `fetch_scr.sh`, `rank.py`, `pead.py`, `s2check.sh`):
- 1,547 symbols, all priced; **809** in ₹1,000–20,000 cr; financials removed 29 (index) + 39 (hand) → **741 eligible**.
- Sample of 120 drawn (first ten: ADFFOODS JINDALPHOT OMAXE SEJALLTD HATHWAY ARVIND RENUKA MAXESTATES EVEREADY UFBL). All 120 pages and
  schedules fetched (HTTP 200); none had a financing-format P&L.
- 9 had EBITDA_TTM ≤ 0 (JINDALPHOT, OMAXE, BGRENERGY, RTNINDIA, ZOTA, NITCO, MMTC, VIPIND, ABREL) → **111 valid**; median EV/EBITDA 14.75x.
- **Cheapest tercile = 37 names, EV/EBITDA ≤ 11.86x** (tercile median 8.66x), from JSWDULUX 2.51x to TCI 11.86x.
- **Walk order (`Random(20261126)`):** JPPOWER, **AUTOAXLES**, GVPIL, GOODLUCK, TVSSCS, HCC, SESHAPAPER, JINDALSAW, JKTYRE, NRAIL, SANDHAR,
  BALMLAWRIE, NAVA, PANAMAPET, TIMETECHNO, NIITMTS, MOL, IFGLEXPOR, TCI, MSTCLTD, EPL, JSWDULUX, SOMANYCERA, HEIDELBERG, JAYNECOIND, CMSINFO,
  HATHWAY, UDS, UNIPARTS, GUJALKALI, STYRENIX, MONTECARLO, LINCOLN, GANDHAR, CIEINDIA, SKIPPER, STAR.

- (v1.4) **"Hidden value" is not mispricing.** SUNFLAG's Lloyds Metals stake exceeded its market cap, but the 45–61% discount had verified causes (L33).
- (v1.4) **"Cheap" is often peak-cycle.** The cheapest EV/EBITDA tercile drew a truck-axle maker at a record peak (L38).
- (v1.4) **A sales-model change can fake growth** (direct OEM sales replacing a related channel; materials ratio exposes it).
- (v1.4) **Our tails are too thin.** Every card's P(blow-up) was 0.07–0.18× the class base rate before anchoring (L36).
- (v1.4) **Tool notes:** screener's "consolidated" URL can silently show standalone data (quarters marked "(S)"); the NSE pledge API can return 0 rows (use SHP XBRL); `sec_fetch.py frames` per-share units are `USD-per-shares`.
